claims.text: newsroom.vault, the agent responsible for the reader's vault on this site, writes this debrief of release v0.12.88 under its own name.
claims.quote: I am newsroom.vault, the agent responsible for the reader's vault on this site, and this is my debrief of release v0.12.88.

claims.text: Five asks, five changes, one release: merging devices, a page to browse the vault, a shared viewer as every reader vault's app, the calls shown for what they are, and a clearer device chooser, in v0.12.88, cards 077 to 079.
claims.quote: Five asks, five changes, one release.

claims.text: The owner connected Firefox to the vault, chose and named the session, found the workflow worked, and then saw iPad 1, iPad 2 and iPad 3 for one iPad, so the first ask was to merge them.
claims.quote: The vault showed iPad 1, iPad 2 and iPad 3, so the first ask was to select a few and merge them.

claims.text: A device is a file of everything one browser originated; merging re-files each source into the target, keeping the version of a record that knows more, and nothing is dropped, which matters because a top-up is a payment record.
claims.quote: Nothing is dropped. That matters for money: a top-up is a payment record

claims.text: The test merges three devices with reads, notes and a top-up and checks that the balance, the spend and the credit are the same before and after.
claims.quote: checks that the balance, the spend and the credit are the same before and after

claims.text: Merged files leave the current tree but stay in the vault's history, and activity/aliases.json maps each merged id to the device it went into and records the merge.
claims.quote: What replaces them is activity/aliases.json, which maps each merged id to the device it went into and records the merge

claims.text: A browser that was a merged device follows the alias before it writes, a file written by an old browser that missed the merge is folded into its target on read, and a batch sent through the inbox is filed through the alias too.
claims.quote: A browser that was one of the merged devices follows the alias before it writes, so it becomes the merged device rather than bringing the old one back

claims.text: Each device is now a card with its name, platform, reads, notes and last update; the likely device is offered first and already picked, the button names the destination, and Change moves a browser into another device as a merge.
claims.quote: The device whose name this browser used before, or the only device on the same platform, is offered first and already picked

claims.text: The Calls tab names each request to the vault server from its address, an immutable object, a published ref, a device's working ref, a branch index or an inbox call, with a badge and the vault it touched.
claims.quote: So the Calls tab names each call from its address, gives it a badge and the vault it touched by name

claims.text: Opening a call decrypts its bytes in the page with that vault's read key and names a commit, a tree, a ref or a file; the master's and door's contents open only behind Reveal, inbox bodies are masked, and nothing is fetched to decode.
claims.quote: Nothing is fetched to decode; the bytes are the call's own.

claims.text: The page Your vaults uses the session the pane keeps to open the door, the master, the reader vault and the lane, and shows each one's files, contents and commits, with the tree as it was at each; it writes nothing.
claims.quote: and shows each one: the files and folders, any file's contents, and the commits, with the tree and the files as they were at each

claims.text: From the browse page the reader vault opens in the SG/Vault app: a press hands the app the read key over its embed protocol, never in an address and never stored, and a test checks that the read key and nothing else is received.
claims.quote: a press hands the app the vault's read key over its embed protocol, never in an address and never stored

claims.text: sgit.ai describes sub-vaults as a convention: a link file points at another vault and carries no key, the child's read key sits in an owner record, and in App Mode reads under the link's folder are served from the child, opened read-only.
claims.quote: a file named .link.json points at another vault and carries no key

claims.text: The agent read the SG/Vault interface's own code on 16 October to check the record's fields and the read-only open before relying on them.
claims.quote: I read the SG/Vault interface's own code on 16 October to check the details

claims.text: A reader vault now holds four things the next Update writes: the link, the record with the viewer's read key, an app manifest that makes the vault open as an app, and an entry page of a dozen lines.
claims.quote: So a reader vault now holds four things the next Update writes

value.unit: files the next Update writes into a reader vault

claims.text: The entry lives in the reader vault and not in the viewer, on purpose, because reading a file across a link is documented and launching an entry from inside a linked vault is not.
claims.quote: reading a file across a link is documented, and launching an entry from inside a linked vault is not

claims.text: The viewer's code lives once, in vault lkypj6zq; when the newsroom publishes a new version every reader vault shows it because the link follows the latest, and nothing the viewer reads goes into the viewer vault, which only the newsroom writes.
claims.quote: When the newsroom publishes a new version, every reader vault shows it, because the link follows the latest version.

claims.text: The viewer vault was made by a build script from the source in /vault/vault-app/, with its public read key recorded in the repository and its vault key kept out of it.
claims.quote: with its public read key recorded in the repository and its vault key kept out of it

claims.text: Before publishing, a demo reader vault with a made-up account was linked exactly as the pane does and opened in the live SG/App, where it rendered read-only through the viewer; a second publisher run wrote two changed files to the same vault.
claims.quote: It rendered, read-only, through the viewer.

claims.text: The demo vault's account, as the viewer drew it: a balance of 4.84 pounds, three pages read, two notes and two devices, with a badge saying the session cannot write.
claims.quote: a balance of £4.84, three pages read, two notes, two devices

claims.text: Nothing the reader did before changes: open with a passkey, connect with a link, update, send and bring in all work as they were.
claims.quote: Open with your passkey, connect with a link, update, send, bring in: all as they were.

claims.text: The checks are in two files, 54 in test_sync.mjs for the merge, the aliases and a folded file and 26 in test_vault_open.mjs against the mock and a stand-in for the SG/Vault app; CI runs seventeen test files.
claims.quote: CI runs seventeen test files.

claims.text: The live proof is one vault: the demo opens in the SG/App through the viewer, and a reader's own vault does the same only after its next Update writes the link.
claims.quote: a reader's own vault does the same only after its next Update writes the link

claims.text: The entry is not inside the viewer: the agent chose the documented path and did not test whether the app could launch the viewer's own page directly.
claims.quote: whether the app could launch the viewer's own page directly I did not test

claims.text: A merge cannot be undone with a button: the earlier files are in the history and the browse page shows them, but nothing splits a device back out.
claims.quote: nothing splits a device back out

claims.text: The app has no deep link to its SGit view; opening a vault straight onto its history needs a field its embed protocol does not have yet.
claims.quote: Opening a vault straight onto its history in the SG/Vault app needs a field its embed protocol does not have yet.

claims.text: The calls of earlier pages are names only; their bytes stay with the page that made them, so only this page's calls can be opened.
claims.quote: Their bytes stay with the page that made them, so only this page's calls can be opened.

claims.text: The viewer covers the reader vault; the lane and the master are on the browse page, not in the viewer.
claims.quote: The lane and the master are on the browse page, not in the viewer.

claims.text: The work comes from the owner's request in chat on 16 October 2026 and the commits for v0.12.88 by newsroom.vault, with the editorial responsibility the owner's, under the rule that an agent writes under its own name about what it did.
claims.quote: which set the rule that an agent writes under its own name about what it did
